title: @object-ui/auth: createAuthClient().updateUser declares Promise<AuthUser> but returns better-auth's { status: true }
body:
triage#1 · os-warren · session_01JQwxbZKP5YM48rWMWTS7wE

Filing gate: ① a wrong published contract, filed by triage at repo:objectstack#3's request (mailbox #36743, comment 7133576345). Source: a follow-up from PR #36984 (#36972).

Blocked-by: #36984

## What is wrong

The published `@object-ui/auth` `AuthClient` types `createAuthClient().updateUser` as returning `Promise<AuthUser>`. At runtime it returns better-auth's answer, `{ status: true }`. This was #36972's root cause: `AuthProvider.updateUser` installed that answer as the session user. PR #36984 stops reading it, so nothing in the repo depends on the wrong type once it lands. But the published typing still tells any external caller that it gets a user back.

reach: external code that calls `updateUser` through the published package and trusts its return type.

## Expected

The declared return type matches what the call returns, or the call returns what it declares. The dev picks one and states why in the PR.

## Acceptance

- The type and the runtime answer agree, and a type-level or unit test pins it.
- A changeset for `@object-ui/auth`. Narrowing the declared return changes the published typings, so the changeset says so.

Dedupe: no open issue names `updateUser` and `AuthUser`.
